A home Wi-Fi network works by using a router to connect devices to the internet. The router acts as a central hub, directing all the devices to connect to the internet. When a device connects to the internet, it sends a signal to the router, which then routes the signal to the access point.

The access point is a device that connects to the internet and acts as a relay for the signal. It uses radio channels to send the signal to the internet. The signal travels through the air and reaches the internet, where it is received by the devices connected to the access point.

When two devices want to transmit a video stream, they use a protocol called the H.264 video codec. This codec is used to compress and transmit video data, making it more efficient to transmit video over the internet. The video stream is then sent to the access point, which then sends it to the internet.

When two devices transmit at once, they use a technique called "multiplexing." This means that they send the video stream to the access point in multiple packets, each of which is sent to a different device. This allows the devices to transmit the video stream simultaneously, without any interference.
